channel.title: We Them Media
channel.description: Street journalism filmed by the people who live there, published free with the full transcript.

item.title: There's no Black genre: Donna Maywar at the Trenton Book Fair.
item.description: Why dedicate a book fair to the Black writer? Donna Maywar, who owns Classics Used and Rare Books on West Lafayette Street in downtown Trenton with her husband, says: "Black people write every genre.

item.title: The beats behind Ready to Die, in full: Easy Mo Bee at Black and Nobel.
item.description: How long did it take to make Ready to Die? Easy Mo Bee, signing his book at Black and Nobel on South Street in Philadelphia, says: "So it's like 6 songs.

item.title: New Jersey's first true superhero: Eric Cooper at the Trenton Book Fair.
item.description: Why write the nerdy sci-fi nobody expects from us? Eric Cooper, "a born and raised Trenton native in New Jersey," "an author, writer, optician by trade and also chauffeur," says: "Most people don't think that we do the nerdy sci-fi stuff.

item.title: ETHConf: loot boxes are crypto's quiet $100M business.
item.description: At ETHConf in Manhattan, June 2026, Garrett Lee of Hydrex, in crypto his "whole career," describes his exchange simply: "It's a DEX on Base," built to solve "the cold start problem of bootstrapping liquidity" for long-tail assets. Asked what crypto is: "It's money via freedom or freedom via money." Asked what an 80-year-old great aunt should know about it: "She shouldn't.

Its premise: "as African Americans, our quest for power has been misdirected." item.description: At the first ETHConf in Manhattan, June 2026, a software engineer at a traditional finance information company comes to look, not to pitch. Why she came: "I'm personally pretty interested in blockchain and all the cryptocurrency-related topics.

item.description: On Day 2 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, Maceo talks with Danielle Toval, from Houston, at the summit for the second year and on a panel about stablecoins. She defines one simply: "a stable version of a fiat currency," in America "1 to 1 to the USD." item.title: The hope is bigger than the fear: crypto on the Metro.
item.description: On a moving Metro train in Washington, DC, Trey talks about growing up Jamaican and being read as Puerto Rican in America instead. He says people who meet him assume he is Spanish and give him that label before he speaks.

item.title: 12 years in prison, now building legal tech.
item.description: Akeem Rand came to Howard University for Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, where he pitched Pro Se Innovations, a tablet built by his company, Made Investment Group, that gives incarcerated people electronic access to file their own legal motions. item.title: A freshman learns why the dollar is losing value.
item.description: Carmelo, a freshman at Howard University in Washington, DC, studying philosophy, talks with Maceo of We Them Media on Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, held on Howard's campus on 25 September 2026. He explains that he chose philosophy over psychology because he prefers logic and reasoning to the emotional side of things.

item.description: On Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, Maceo Whatley talks with Ingrid Sturgis, who teaches journalism at Howard University's School of Communications and still works as a journalist herself. She describes crypto as a currency owned by no single entity, one she says can be exploited: "It is a casino," and some of the people trading in it are, in her word, "unscrupulous." item.title: Bitcoin as a hedge against a weakening dollar.
item.description: Joseph, who goes by Joe, is a junior at Howard University studying sports management, with a minor in political science. He says he's interested in sports and entertainment law.

item.title: Scam, man: Ricasso on crypto and inflation.
item.description: On Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, Maceo sits down at Howard University with Eric Holder, known as Ricasso, a painter and muralist in DC. Ricasso talks first about the mural scene: opportunities "range and vary, just depending on how much you applying, how much you really doing.

item.title: The biggest question of 2026.
item.description: On Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, Maceo sits down on the Howard University campus in Washington, DC, with Amaziah Williams, a broadcast journalism major with a philosophy minor, born and raised in DC. Amaziah traces his path to journalism back to his great-grandmother, who graduated from Howard in 1943, and to sports broadcasting he picked up in high school.

item.title: Comfortable in her Blackness: a senior's story.
item.description: Molina Diaz is a senior at Howard University, studying philosophy and sociology, from Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Filmed on Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, Howard University, Washington, DC, 25 September 2026.

item.title: A DAO for Black liberation, and the petrodollar.
item.description: Milan came to Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026 at Howard University after seeing an ad on Facebook. He is not a Howard student.

item.title: A computer science student learns Bitcoin.
item.description: On Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, at Howard University in Washington, DC, Maceo sits down with Chris, a computer science sophomore from New Jersey. Chris says he does not know much about crypto: "I would say it's like a source of money." item.title: A pre-med student on why Black doctors matter.
item.description: At Howard University in Washington, DC, on Day 1 of the Black Blockchain Summit 2026, Maceo sits down with Rosh, a Howard second-year majoring in biology on the pre-med track. Rosh, who is from Chicago, explains why he wants to become a Black surgeon: Black doctors make up only 4 percent of the field, he says, and he wants to be part of changing that.

item.title: Russ and Sirsu in Manhattan: use every resource at your disposal.
item.description: A walk through Manhattan at night and a long table afterwards, with Maceo filming: Worldwide Russ and Sirsu interview each other about what New York taught them. Russ sets it up: "I want to talk with people who made it in New York".

item.title: In the Same Room: it's always, always about impact.
item.description: Bayo, on his way to In the Same Room, the Pentecost Art Club event in Abuja, stops the club's founder at the door: "We're heading out right now for the Pentecost Art Club event called In the Same Room. How you feeling, brother?" The founder introduces himself as Pentecost the Preacher.

item.title: ETHConf: blockchain en más de 40 universidades argentinas.
item.description: An Argentine at ETHConf in New York is working to get more people across Latin America, governments and schools above all, to learn and understand blockchain. In Spanish.
